campaign: MOSS in overgo does what the MOSS Ultra workflow does in ComfyUI, each section held to ComfyUI's recording

items.title: LiveEdit's scorecard row carries a time at the size a person asks for: an edit of a clip at 832 x 480

steps.title: An edit's request at a person's size is its page's own size with a source clip at that size, and LiveEdit's page states its developers' size
steps.rationale:
The owner's review of 2026-11-25, point 3, checked by the lead against the closing run's log: valid. LiveEdit's video-user-size cell (22/105) measured nothing: "the verification of ... LiveEdit states no size of its own, so there is no larger request to measure" (mediacapability.PersonRequest found no default size on its page and a size its runtime does not fill), so its only time is the 32 x 16 request's, 12.0 s in that run. The model runs at 832 x 480, the size it was trained at: the README's sample, 33 frames of the Wan clip at that size, was drawn in 25 s on 2026-11-25.

The change: LiveEdit's page declares its developers' size and frames (read them from its model card and inference code), and an edit's request at a person's size takes its source clip at that size too, the stored Wan clip (file:sha256:aba27ea7...) or one the verification names, so the size timed is a size a person edits at. Then the cell is measured on the card (go run ./cmd/validate -run -model LiveEdit), and the scorecard row carries the time.

Check: TestAnEditAtAPersonsSizeTakesASourceAtThatSize, PersonRequest of LiveEdit's module: the request is lifted to the page's size with a source clip of that size; it calls PersonRequest, which the base holds, so it builds there and fails on its assertion.

decisions.question: skill.md's 227 rule lines each cite a check. Read at 3ba4de8c7: the first check of 181 has a doc comment and of 45 has none, and the comments state what their test holds, not the rule that cites it ("purpose = recursive self-improvement ..." cites TestCycleFilesDeclinesAndAcceptsNothing, whose comment is the cycle's comparisons; "scorecard columns = ..." cites TestScorecardRowsEveryServableModel, whose comment is rows and dashes). Writing skill.md from the comments as they stand changes what it says. Which form does skill.md take?
options: Each rule line moves onto its first check as a doc-comment line of its own, and skill.md is generated from those lines and its judgement section, so it says what it says now, each rule written once on its check
skill.md holds its terms and judgement lines alone; the rule lines go, each check saying its rule when it refuses
skill.md is written from the tests' doc comments as they stand, its wording changing to theirs
decisions.recommendation: Each rule line moves onto its first check as a doc-comment line of its own, and skill.md is generated from those lines and its judgement section, so it says what it says now, each rule written once on its check
